title: payment.settled.v1
description: Settlement of a captured payment was OBSERVED in a gateway report. Published by Ledger & Reconciliation (BC-8) - not by the orchestrator - on pp.payments.payment.v1, keyed by payment_id, because settlement is observed from gateway reports rather than decided by us. The platform takes no custody of funds and does not compute settlement: every figure here is as REPORTED, and a gross/fee/net arithmetic mismatch opens a reconciliation exception rather than being silently corrected.

feeAmount.description: The gateway fee as reported. We do not compute it.

netAmount.description: gross - fee, as reported. A mismatch with our own subtraction opens a reconciliation exception; it is never silently corrected, because a report we quietly 'fix' is a report we can no longer reconcile against.

settlementCurrency.description: May differ from the payment currency on cross-currency settlement.

fxRate.description: Present only on cross-currency settlement. A DECIMAL STRING, not a float and not Money - it is a rate rather than an amount, and its precision matters in a way that binary floating point cannot preserve.

settlementDate.description: The value date the gateway reports, as a calendar date rather than an instant - settlement is a banking-day concept, not a timestamp.

reportUri.description: The ingested gateway report, retained so a disputed figure can be traced to the bytes we received.

observedAt.description: When WE observed the settlement, distinct from settlementDate. The gap between the two is the reconciliation lag.
